results.draft_answer:
The significance of the statement "A person can be highly educated, professionally successful, and financially illiterate" is that it explains why many people struggle financially despite their professional achievements [Page 51]. 

According to the provided text, this condition occurs because schools focus on scholastic and professional skills rather than financial skills [Page 12]. Consequently, even highly educated individuals—such as bankers, doctors, and accountants—may graduate with a "poor person's financial programming and mind-set" [Page 12]. 

The specific implications of this financial illiteracy include:
* **Lack of Cash Flow Understanding:** Most people struggle because they do not understand cash flow [Page 51].
* **Mismanagement of Money:** These individuals have not learned how to spend money, how to keep it, or how to make their money work for them [Page 51, 52].
* **Unnecessary Hard Work:** Because they only learned how to work hard rather than how to have their money work for them, these individuals often work harder than they need to [Page 51, 52].
* **Vulnerability:** Financial illiteracy, defined as an inability to read numbers or words regarding money, is the foundation of financial struggle [Page 49].
results.final_output: The significance of the statement 'A person can be highly educated, professionally successful, and financially illiterate' is that it highlights a disconnect between academic success and financial aptitude [Page 51, Page 12].
results.final_answer: The significance of the statement 'A person can be highly educated, professionally successful, and financially illiterate' is that it highlights a disconnect between academic success and financial aptitude [Page 51, Page 12].

Time management is critical in building wealth because time is considered your "most precious asset" [Page 106]. The choices you make regarding how you spend your time, along with your money and what you put in your head, are daily decisions that determine your financial future [Page 106]. 

Furthermore, time management is identified as one of the three most important management skills necessary for starting a business and living your life effectively, whether as an individual, a family member, or within an organization [Page 111, 112]. Mastering this skill, alongside the management of cash flow and people, is enhanced by the mastery of self-discipline [Page 112].
